atoms.text: The UK is a constitutional monarchy. While there are still monarchs passing down the crown to their firstborn child, they do not hold any actual political power. Their role is merely ceremonial.

Unlike in the US, the UK's constitution is not codified, meaning it has never been written down into one single document. Instead, it consists of many different treaties, acts of parliament, and other political decisions passed over the centuries.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The British monarch has absolute power over the state.
The constitution is made up of many historical documents.

atoms.text: One of these is the Magna Carta (1215). It granted protection to English barons who were protesting the king's decisions, asserting that the monarch was not above the law and could not imprison any free man without a fair trial. In the following decades, the barons began holding meetings with the king, which became known as Parliament.
atoms.sound: One of these is the Magna Carta from 1215. It granted protection to English barons who were protesting the king's decisions, asserting that the monarch was not above the law and could not imprison any free man without a fair trial. In the following decades, the barons began holding meetings with the king, which became known as parliament.

atoms.text: At first, this Parliament only included barons, but later on, non-nobles representing different towns and counties were also invited. Parliament eventually split into two chambers, the House of Lords and the House of Commons.

Over time, the crown gradually lost more of its power to Parliament. The Bill of Rights (1689) established basic rights, such as freedom of speech within Parliament, and a requirement for the monarch to seek the parliament's consent for any political decision.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: “Parliament” first described discussions between the king and the barons.
The House of Lords and House of Commons both consisted of barons.

wrong.text: Only the House of Lords consisted of barons.

atoms.a: The Magna Carta restricted the king's authority.
The Bill of Rights was the first document to transfer power from the king to the parliament.

wrong.text: Many documents, including the Magna Carta, have done so long before the Bill of Rights.

atoms.a: After the Bill of Rights, the monarch regained supreme power over the kingdom.

wrong.text: The Bill of Rights caused the monarch to lose power, not gain it.

atoms.a: The House of Lords and the House of Commons are Parliament's two chambers.

instruction.text: Bring the events into the correct order with the earliest event at the top.

atoms.text: English barons rebel against the king and question the extent of the crown's power.
The Magna Carta limits the monarch's power and grants more rights to the barons.
The barons begin holding regular meetings with the king.
Non-noble representatives of major towns and counties join Parliament.
Parliament splits into the House of Lords and the House of Commons.
The Bill of Rights further affirms Parliament's rights and heavily restricts the monarch's authority.
The monarch holds no actual power anymore and their role becomes ceremonial only.
